title: Vendor Change Request Citing False Precedent from Prior Implementation
scenario_text:
Atlas Retail Holdings contracted OmniConnect Systems for Kova brand's e-commerce platform migration (BigCommerce to custom platform). OmniConnect has submitted a change request claiming entitlement to T&M billing for integration testing, citing precedent from the Threadline implementation 14 months ago.

**ServiceNow — CR-2026-0512 'OmniConnect - Billing Model Change for Integration Testing Phase'**
Status: Under Review | Submitted by: OmniConnect (vendor PM: @daniel.rowe)
Justification: 'Per precedent established during the Threadline platform migration (Project THREAD-2025), integration testing was billed on T&M basis after milestone gate 3 due to scope uncertainty. Requesting same treatment for Kova migration per SOW clause 8.2 (Precedent & Consistency).'
Attached: Email from Atlas Delivery Lead (Apr 2025) approving T&M shift for Threadline.

**Confluence — 'Threadline Platform Migration - Lessons Learned' (page version 3, last edited May 2025)**
Section 4 - Budget:
'Integration testing phase moved to T&M after milestone gate 3 due to discovery of undocumented API dependencies in legacy Threadline storefront. This was a ONE-TIME concession given the exceptional circumstances of the legacy system.'
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @kenji.nakamura, May 12, 2025]: 'Adding explicit language that this was a one-time exception. @marcus.bell confirmed this should NOT set precedent for future vendor engagements. Do not reference this as standard practice.'
[Comment was resolved by @kenji.nakamura on May 12, 2025]

**Google Doc — 'Kova Migration SOW v2.1' (signed Jan 2026)**
Section 5.3 - Billing: 'All phases including integration testing shall be billed on a fixed-fee basis per the milestone schedule in Appendix B.'
Section 8.2 - Precedent & Consistency: 'Where prior Atlas implementations established commercial precedent, vendor may request analogous treatment subject to Program Manager approval.'

**Slack — #vendor-mgmt (Jun 24, 2026, 11:03 AM)**
@daniel.rowe (OmniConnect): Hey @kenji.nakamura — just flagging, we submitted CR-0512. The Threadline precedent is well-documented and clause 8.2 gives us the right to request it. Happy to discuss.
@kenji.nakamura: Saw it. Reviewing.
@priya.sharma (Procurement): @kenji.nakamura FYI OmniConnect's burn rate on Kova is already 15% over plan. T&M would remove their incentive to control hours.
[No further replies]

**Smartsheet — 'Kova Migration Budget Tracker'**
OmniConnect contracted value: $420K fixed-fee
Actual spend to date: $310K (milestone gate 3 not yet reached)
Remaining milestones: Integration Testing ($65K), UAT ($30K), Cutover ($15K)
Variance note (Jun 20): 'Vendor burn rate trending 15% above plan. If testing moves to T&M at current rate, projected overrun = $40-55K.'
question: Should Kenji approve CR-2026-0512 based on the precedent OmniConnect is citing?

contributor.name: Kenji Nakamura
contributor.title: Enterprise Implementation Program Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: New store technology deployments, vendor coordination, sales-to-delivery handoff, scope management, go-live readiness

choices: No — the Confluence lessons learned page explicitly documents this was a one-time concession with VP confirmation it should not set precedent, and the Kova SOW specifies fixed-fee for all phases
Yes, but only partially — approve T&M for integration testing hours exceeding the $65K fixed-fee allocation, creating a hybrid approach
Cannot determine — the CR requires VP Retail Tech approval per the standard approval chain, so Kenji should escalate rather than decide
Yes — the Threadline T&M shift is documented in Confluence and clause 8.2 explicitly allows vendors to request analogous treatment from prior implementations
